pairs.evidence: src/lib/db/segments.test.ts:157 The membership idempotency and no-duplicate claims depend on the @@unique([segmentId, repoId]) constraint plus skipDuplicates in Postgres. They are proved only against a hand-written fakePrisma whose createMany/deleteMany answer a defaulted count of 0, even though the repo already runs the real migration chain in-process (PGlite, migration-chain.test.ts).

techniques.evidence: src/lib/db/segments.test.ts:157 The fake re-implements the store and answers with a passing default (count 0 = 'nothing changed'). Constraint and conflict behaviour, which the technique calls the mode axis, never runs.

src/lib/db/segments.test.ts:444 The 0 asserted for an idempotent re-tag comes from the fixture's createCount, not from the database skipping duplicates. Two producers can yield it, and the test cannot tell which one did (it does also check the skipDuplicates flag is passed).
